what_happened: The design job "Design direct-to-main landing to retire the long-lived landing branch" was rejected at the final verdict. The job changed docs only. One acceptance criterion was unmet: the one that says cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test each pass, or Athena's recorded check on the same tree passed. The verifier also raised one major finding: behavior criterion 7 is unmet because its evidence must cite commands that ran (D43). One check failed, the test check. Shard 3 of 6 reported that 1 of 14 units failed, athena-cli --test drain. The kept output shows only passing tests from another crate and the CI error line, so the failing test is not visible. A docs-only change breaking a drain test suggests the failure was pre-existing, flaky or caused by something else, but the fields do not say which.
cause: A repo-wide test check was made a criterion for a docs-only design job, and nothing recorded whether the same test fails on the base tree. When the drain test failed, the job was rejected on the check and on the evidence rule (D43), and nothing separated a failure the job caused from one that was already there. The kept output was CI noise from another crate, so the failing test and its assertion could not be seen. A design job that changes only docs has no way to show that the failure is unrelated to its change.
other_causes: The criterion asks for evidence that the verifier can only accept if it cites commands that ran, and this made the rule-D43 finding a second rejection for the same missing evidence.
The kept test output holds the last lines of a different crate's run, not the failing athena-cli drain test, so the failure was invisible to the producer, verifier and the person running Athena.
open_hypotheses: The drain test failure may be pre-existing on main, which the fields cannot confirm or rule out.
The drain test may be flaky or timing-dependent, and a rerun might pass.
The docs change may touch a file that a drain test reads, such as a pinned digest or a generated view.
contradictions: The job changed only docs, yet a code test failed, which points against the job having caused the failure.
Earlier cases in the design-job class (20261026-061735-8rvt) were rejected on verifier findings about the note's content, not on a failed check, so they do not match this event.
prevention: When a check fails on a job whose diff touches only docs, Athena should automatically run the same failing test on the base tree. It should record the result: failing on base means pre-existing, and the job is judged on its criteria with the check marked as not caused by it. The test check should also keep the failing test's name and assertion output instead of CI cleanup lines. For docs-only jobs, the recorded check on an unchanged code tree should count as the evidence for the fmt, clippy and test criterion, so that criterion does not depend on the producer running commands.
proposed_request: Make a failed test check on a docs-only job diagnosable and judged against a baseline. (1) When the test check fails and the job's diff touches no code or test files, rerun the failing unit, for example `athena-cli --test drain`, on the base tree, and record whether it also fails there. (2) If it also fails on base, record the check as pre-existing and judge the job's acceptance criteria normally. If it passes on base, keep it as a real failure and name the failing test. (3) Keep the failing test name and assertion text in the kept check output, not only the last CI lines. Acceptance: a test with a fixture where a docs-only diff meets a failing test that also fails on base is judged on its criteria. A fixture where the test fails only with the diff is still rejected. The kept output names the failing test. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
